name: Higashiyama
description: Kyoto's Higashiyama: Kiyomizu-dera's wooden stage over the valley, the stone lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka with their noren and lanterns, and the Yasaka Pagoda over the roofs.

water.note: No sea: Kyoto is 25-80 m above it. The ponds (Maruyama Park's, the temples') are drawn at their own level (inland, pipeline/inland_water.py); the hill streams are left to the photograph.

inland.note: Ponds at the 5 m laser survey's level.
inland.skip_note: The Keage purification plant's distribution reservoirs are covered tanks.

roofs.note: pipeline/arcades.py: a precinct whose roofs on posts and gates take its own colour (Kiyomizu-dera's gates and pavilions are vermilion, though it is a temple)

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from Kyoto's street-tree surveys and the temples' own guides. The streets have zelkovas (keyaki), ginkgos, camphors and cherries; the Higashiyama hillsides are a laurel forest of evergreen oaks and chinquapins (evergreen) with cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too), black pines and maples. Areas give the precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own: Kiyomizu-dera's thousand maples and fifteen hundred cherries, Maruyama Park's cherries round the Gion weeping cherry, Kodai-ji's maples. Their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py).

areas.name: Kiyomizu-dera
areas.note: About a thousand maples and fifteen hundred cherries round the Stage and down the Nishikigumo valley.

areas.name: Gion weeping cherry
areas.note: Maruyama Park's Gion shidarezakura (the second, grown from the first's seed), about 12 m tall, planted on its own spot as a landmark tree (city.py gion_cherry, landmarks.json trees): the lone round crown in the plaza in the aerial photograph.

areas.name: Maruyama Park
areas.note: Kyoto's oldest public park, famous for its cherries round the Gion weeping cherry: about 680, Somei-yoshino and weeping cherries (the park's guide).

areas.name: Kodai-ji
areas.note: Kodai-ji's weeping cherry before the Hojo's rock garden, and its maples.

protection.title: No statutory sun rule for public places
protection.summary: Kyoto protects its skyline with height limits (a cap of 31 m in the busiest districts) and Japan limits shadows on homes with the Building Standards Act, but neither protects sun on parks. Sun on these places is measured for information, not tested against a rule.
protection.source_note: No legal window is transcribed for these places, so each is shown for 10:00-14:00 and none is marked protected.
protection.reading_note: Heights come from Project PLATEAU, measured from aerial survey in 2020-2021, so buildings finished since are missing or low.
protection.tip: Tip: the hillside puts the lanes in shade early on winter afternoons.

kiyomizu.note: Kiyomizu-dera, Kiyomizu-zaka, Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka and the Yasaka Pagoda: pipeline/osm_detail.py

tour.title: Old Kyoto on the hillside
tour.text: The lanes climb from Yasaka-dori to the gates of Kiyomizu-dera, past teahouses, pottery shops and pickle sellers. Come early, before the tour buses, or at dusk when the lanterns come on.

tour.title: Kiyomizu-dera
tour.text: The Main Hall's stage hangs nearly 13 m over the valley on a lattice of keyaki pillars, joined without a single nail. "To jump from the stage of Kiyomizu" is how Kyoto says taking the plunge.

tour.title: Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka
tour.text: Stone steps between two-storey wooden shops, noren in the doorways, lanterns at the eaves. Legend says a stumble on Sannenzaka brings three years' bad luck, so watch your step.

tour.title: The Yasaka Pagoda
tour.text: Five storeys of bare timber, 46 m high, rebuilt in 1440: the picture of Kyoto, at the top of the lane, best framed from Yasaka-dori at sunset.

game.title: Higashiyama on Foot

travel.name: Gion: Yasaka Shrine 八坂神社

game.blurb: Walk Higashiyama under the real sun: up Yasaka-dori to the pagoda, through the stone lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, to the stage of Kiyomizu-dera and the view Conan fans come for.

npcs.name: Aiko 愛子
idle: Half the girls in kimono on these lanes rented them from a shop like mine. The other half are from Kyoto and laugh at us.
Dusk is the hour: the lanterns come on and the pagoda goes dark against the sky.

npcs.name: Mr. Fujii 藤井
idle: Kiyomizu-yaki: pottery from these slopes since the 1600s. Chawan-zaka, the Teapot Lane, is named for it.
Mind your step on Sannenzaka. They say if you fall here you'll be unlucky for three years.

npcs.name: Ryosen 良仙
idle: The Deva Gate is the temple's red front door. The two guardians: one with his mouth open, one closed. A and Un, the beginning and the end.

npcs.name: Mika 美香
npcs.role: Detective Conan fan on a pilgrimage
idle: 真実はいつもひとつ! One truth prevails. I've done Gojo Ohashi and Rokkaku-do already; Kiyomizu is the big one.
The view I need is from the Okunoin: the whole stage on its pillars, like in the film.

lines.title: The pagoda at dusk
lines.on_open: Both walks done. Go back down to Aiko on Yasaka-dori, below the pagoda.

quests.title: The pagoda at the top of the street
talk: おこしやす, welcome to Higashiyama. That's the Yasaka Pagoda: five storeys, 46 m, rebuilt in 1440. Every photo of Kyoto has it somewhere.
Before you climb, look at the coloured charms at Koshin-do, just here: Conan fans know them. WASD to walk, Shift to run, E to talk.
After that, two walks, either one first: the stone lanes, where Mr. Fujii keeps a pottery shop on Sannenzaka, and the temple, where Ryosen waits at the red gate.

steps.text: See the kukurizaru at Yasaka Koshin-do

quests.title: Three years' luck
talk: Ah, a visitor. These lanes have been preserved by law since 1976: the stone, the wooden fronts, the lattices, no tall signs.
Climb the steps outside to the top, and mind your feet. Then come back down and turn into Ninenzaka, the quieter lane. Look at the fronts, not the shops.

steps.text: Climb the steps of Sannenzaka to the top
Walk back down and into Ninenzaka

quests.title: The red gate
talk: Welcome to Kiyomizu-dera, the Temple of Pure Water. Founded in 778; the halls you see were rebuilt in 1633.
A young pilgrim was asking for the stage. Go through the gate and past the pagoda; she is by the water basin.

steps.text: Find Mika in the temple precinct

quests.title: One truth prevails
talk: You're going to the stage too? Kiyomizu is in Crossroad in the Ancient Capital, and in Crimson School Trip Shinichi and Ran have their photo taken here.
Stand on the stage first, then cross to the Okunoin for the photo. The Otowa Falls are below it: drink from one stream, not three.

steps.text: Stand on the Stage of Kiyomizu
Take the photo from the Okunoin's stage

quests.title: After dark
talk: おかえりやす. Up to the temple and down again in one piece: no falls on Sannenzaka, I hope.
Now wait for the best part. When the sun has gone, the lanterns come on along the street and the pagoda goes dark against the sky. Stand in the road just below it and look up.

steps.text: Stand on Yasaka-dori below the pagoda after dark
